limits: All ten maps were previously examined; map-level means do not create an independent specimen sample.
The device crosswalk is unavailable. Spatial intervals are conditional within-map resampling ranges, not device-level confidence intervals.

Block side is based on the isotropic triangular moire-cell area approximation from each map's median same-family wall-row spacing; it is a sensitivity scale, not a measured spatial correlation length.
Camera, probe and window checks are sensitivity analyses on the same walls; they are not independent replications.

population.v002_width_cohort: Width summaries use measured and all four relaxed candidates qualified in both rings. Rigid qualification is counted separately. Full-profile score coverage keeps every finite original-cohort wall regardless of width qualification.

primary_spatial_block_sensitivity.limits: Percentile ranges describe conditional within-map spatial sensitivity with fitted registration and optical calibration fixed. Scans may share specimens/devices; no device crosswalk is available, so these are not device-level confidence intervals and do not include acquisition, camera, probe or model uncertainty.
primary_spatial_block_sensitivity.scope: Resample square clusters of wall midpoint scores within each fixed scan, pairing anchor and candidate score on each resampled wall; average map means with equal scan weights. Four half-block origin phases are combined.

same_wall_across_settings.definition: Original-cohort wall midpoints with finite two-direction scores for anchor and every candidate in every available camera/probe/window condition; identical walls are used within each map for all settings.

score_definition: transfer_error is the saved Euclidean norm of the selected per-reflection detrended unit shapes, with ring channel-count normalization, after fitting position in the source direction. Values are used directly; they are dimensionless.

synthetic_anchor_render.interpretation: These are noiseless forward-rendered anchor profiles measured with the short-window observer, compared with the saved intrinsic midpoint slip-gradient FWHM. They isolate window/probe response; they are not repeated experimental measurements or a barrier recovery test.
